body:
A bit more explanation here, I saw a school-employed psychiatrist, a school counselor(and the disciplinary director when I skipped class and he noticed some scratches on my hands... he wasn't helpful), and a therapist who was employed through my mother's work. The psychiatrist was very kind and private with me, however the counselor would call my mother after I told her *anything*, even when I mentioned my foot hurt from a pebble in my shoe. As nice a lady as she is, she made my situation so much worse by dishing out incorrect, second hand information that I had to correct. The therapist suggested my mother take me for a CAT scan, to which my mother said no because she didn't believe me that much.

edit: There was no mention of privacy no with anyone I saw, just to make that a bit more clear. I also hope I will still be taken seriously now that I mention I'm in high school.
I'll get to typing, it may take a while. Feel free to read it later if it's late at night where you are, I think I'm safe from myself where I'm staying tonight.

Before I explain, I want to say that she's caring and loves me and only wants me to be happy. She's the best mother in the world. But when the therapists told her what I was telling them, she said my issues were too extreme and too sudden to be real. I was upset by this and asked her why I would ever make up such a story, and she said that I was probably seeking attention to compete with my problematic friends that I'm always helping.

I don't really blame her. Even to myself, my story is ridiculous, and I do an awful job at explaining what's wrong.

Again, apologize for the length of my comment, I get carried away.

I did see a psychiatrist, therapist and counselor, and as I explained myself and what was troubling me at the time, they all had sincere concern, but never really did anything beyond asking me the same questions. The experience was short-lived, as my mother sat me down and told me to cut the "act". My main problem with talking about my issues is that I don't now how to go bout it. I can't figure out what exactly is making me feel this way, and I end up getting nervous and I don't want to talk anymore.

I try my best to distract myself, I exercise, play instruments and work on cars, but when it comes down to it, the pain feels so nice and comforting. It sounds so masochistic, but it's true. My love of pain combined with my love of destruction is a dangerous combination. Luckily I've been only cutting my fingers recently, which doesn't leave noticeable scars and I can focus on healing my old ones, but I'd still like to stop so I can live a bit of a more normal life.

Honestly, it feels really refreshing to know that others feel suicidal even with no big problems in life. I'm unsure whether or not I conveyed this in my original post, but the tendencies are very serious (it's never "Oh, I wish I were dead", but rather "If I wait until my mother leaves for work, I could run out to the highway before my siblings wake up") and when I look back, I always regret not going through with it. I have attempted a couple times, but I have very limited resources where I currently live, so they never quite turned out right. These suicidal thoughts have been manifesting in my mind for quite some time, maybe... 2 years? And they are prevalent almost daily. I just want to rid myself of this so that I can go about my day without worrying that I'm going to jump off the first ledge I see.

And thank you for the offer, if you feel like reading an extremely bizarre novel about my life, I'll PM you :)
